profiles.label: Stanford GSB · Social Media Manager
profiles.headline: The next great campus story starts with a conversation.
profiles.summary: I’m Gabriel: a builder, interviewer and community founder with a computer science background. I want to bring my curiosity, hands-on content production and analytical approach to Stanford GSB’s Social Media Manager role.
motivation: The part that draws me in is being present: meeting people, asking good questions and noticing the story behind what they are building. In San Francisco and New York in November 2026, I attended hackathons, spoke with founders and filmed team interviews. I enjoy finding those stories in person.

Corvus lets me connect the whole journey: build a community experience, document it, publish it and inspect the response. I would bring that practical mindset to campus coverage while learning the school’s editorial standards and working closely with its communications team.

proposal: Listen first: meet the team and campus partners, review channel performance, voice guidelines, approvals and escalation practices.
Plan and pilot: build a small editorial calendar around real campus events; capture interviews and test accessible, platform-native formats with the team.
Review and improve: report on reach, engagement and website actions, share lessons and refine the next set of stories.

profiles.label: UC Berkeley · academic profile
profiles.headline: Build things. Question the systems behind them.
profiles.summary: I’m exploring a next step that brings computer science, philosophy and human–AI interaction together. I have a BSc in Computer Science, experience building products and course research on LLMs and human behaviour.
motivation: Working with AI every day has changed how I learn and what I question. I want to understand how AI influences human judgement, how people assign agency to these systems and how to evaluate the tools we build.

Berkeley is one of the places I want to explore for that next chapter. My starting point is a conversation about the right academic fit, supported by my transcripts, research writing and working projects.
interests: Human–AI interaction: influence, agency and the quality of human judgement.
AI-assisted learning: what helps people understand, rather than simply complete a task.
Building and evaluating public-facing software with real users.

profiles.label: Harvard · academic profile
profiles.headline: From making software to thinking about its consequences.
profiles.summary: My route into philosophy grew out of working with AI. I want to connect my computer science background and experience building a community with deeper work on judgement, agency and the social consequences of technology.
profiles.motivationTitle: The questions I want to pursue
motivation: My AI workflow over the past month has made me think like a philosopher. It wasn’t a deliberate choice, but a path I found myself on and enjoy taking. Building tools has made questions about knowledge, responsibility and influence feel concrete.

I’m exploring Harvard as a possible next academic chapter. I would like to find the right setting to sharpen those questions through careful argument, research and conversation, while continuing to build.
interests: How AI tools shape what we believe, decide and create.
Responsibility and agency in human–AI collaboration.
How communities learn, share knowledge and evaluate the quality of ideas.
